dossier.architecture: Offset shooter and cargo path leave room for a central rotating climber.

subsystems.drivetrain: Swerve; exact module model not established here.
subsystems.intake: Wide compliant collection into an offset tunnel.
subsystems.transfer: Independent front and rear elevator belts oppose to store cargo and run together to feed; rear rejection uses color and infrared sensing.
subsystems.scoring: Fixed-heading adjustable-hood launcher; added back rollers and a between-regionals ball stop. Remote motor placement counterbalances the offset scorer.
subsystems.endgame: Central rear-deploying rotary system, steel clips and center-of-gravity transfer; guide flap helped clearance in a triple climb with 254.
subsystems.controls: Prime button roughly aims chassis before Limelight correction; dashboard/LEDs report cargo and ready state.

versions: Ball stop added between regional events.
Worlds used a compatible two-ball autonomous alongside 254's five-ball; later three-ball discussion is not evidence of that Worlds routine. Chezy interview is postseason.
dossier.analysis: This is an alliance-fit example: a robot can deliberately use a smaller autonomous routine to preserve a stronger partner's route. Packaging the climber centrally shaped both intake and shooter placement.
limits: Only the reviewed published configurations are established; intermediate changes may be undocumented.

context_documents.title: 2022-1619 · An offset path changes both cargo control and partner climb clearance
context_documents.body:
# 2022-1619: An offset path changes both cargo control and partner climb clearance

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

Separate front/rear elevator belts oppose to retain cargo and run together to feed an offset fixed-heading launcher. Color/IR staging supports rear rejection. A driver alignment flap helps place the robot for a shared hangar climb.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The source explicitly connects the alignment cue to preventing a climb motor from hitting the hangar wall during a triple climb.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Transport modes must preserve possession while another action waits on readiness. The offset scorer and climb envelope also affect alliance geometry; a theoretically fast independent climb may collide in a three-robot arrangement.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test retention during belt reversals and verify shared-climb clearance with representative partners, not only an isolated fixture.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://youtu.be/MlXF9CxDrlg](https://youtu.be/MlXF9CxDrlg)

source_reviews.title: Behind the Bumpers with Up-A-Creek Robotics at Chezy Champs
source_reviews.locator: 1:13–3:42 collection and routing; 3:44–5:42 balance and launcher; 6:12–8:47 climb; 8:48–10:57 controls
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the full available English automatic caption track, including the start and end. Technical details are attributed to team speakers. No visual inspection claimed.
facts: The wide collector routes laterally to an off-center tunnel. Independent elevator drives oppose to retain cargo and run together to feed.
Two elevator gearboxes, the shooter gearbox and flywheel were moved across the chassis to counterbalance the offset shooter.
The central rotary climb deploys from the rear and locks out with spring-steel latches. A flexible alignment cue protects the motor near the hangar wall.
source_reviews.limitations: The interview took place after Worlds. The team distinguished the two-cargo Worlds routine from later autonomous discussion. The reported nine-second climb is a best case.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Vertigo’s central climber set the overall layout. The team wanted to hang from either side of the bay, so the shooter and cargo elevator went to the side and part of their drive mass went across the chassis. This made the robot’s lateral balance a deliberate design decision. The same packaging choice also gives the collector an extra job: moving a ball from almost anywhere across the front into a side entrance.
piece_flow: The compliant collector sends cargo inward and laterally. Beam breaks and color sensing coordinate staging and rear rejection.
Front and rear elevator belt sets run against one another to hold accepted cargo, or move together to carry it upward.
A blocker prevents early entry and backing rollers help maintain shot consistency. The chassis turns to aim the fixed-heading, adjustable-hood launcher.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: Power crosses the frame through shafts and belts from mass moved away from the launcher. The driven components must remain aligned even when the frame sees an offset hit. The central climb folds from the rear and changes robot attitude during rung transfers. Partner and wall clearances therefore depend on the entire swing, including protruding motors.

subsystems.name: Offset pickup and sorting
subsystems.construction: Flexible wide intake, lateral centering wheels, offset tunnel, beam breaks and a rear reject path.
subsystems.operation: Draw cargo toward one side, read its state and pass it upward or out the back.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team prioritized retaining a ball on contact and tested several pickup rung spacings.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: An off-center throat creates different travel lengths from opposite edges, so center-only tests hide the limiting handoff.
subsystems.interfaces: The reject path and deployed climber both occupy the rear region at different times.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Run fast approaches from both edges with a queued ball already present. Inspect lateral guide positions after contact.
subsystems.unknowns: Exact wheel geometry and rejection timing were not established.

subsystems.name: Opposing-belt elevator
subsystems.construction: Separate gearboxes run the front and rear belt surfaces independently.
subsystems.operation: Oppose the surfaces to retain the ball and run both up to feed it.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team uses the two drive directions to select storage or delivery.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Holding with opposing motion uses active contact and can spin or creep the ball if compression is asymmetric. Verify the transition to upward motion after a brownout or reversal.
subsystems.interfaces: Sensor state and the launcher blocker must agree on whether the ball is held, moving or already at the wheel.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check wear, belt tension mismatch and false occupancy with the elevator full.
subsystems.unknowns: No measured drift, current or stop behavior.

subsystems.name: Offset launcher and chassis aim
subsystems.construction: Adjustable hood, later back rollers and ball stop. Belts and shafts couple displaced mass to the mechanisms.
subsystems.operation: Prime toward the hub using a coarse estimate, apply camera correction and feed the fixed heading shooter.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team describes reducing speed variation between shots and preventing premature feeds.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Remote mass can improve static balance but adds shafts, bearing alignment and service work. Aim calibration must account for the muzzle’s offset from the robot reference.
subsystems.interfaces: Drive motion, vision, ball stop and release speed jointly set repeatability.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect shaft alignment after frame impact and test loss of vision between prime and release.
subsystems.unknowns: Full mass properties, hood range and speed recovery are unresolved.

subsystems.name: Central rotary climb
subsystems.construction: Rear fold-out rotary structure with pneumatic deployment, spring-steel latches and a flexible visual alignment flap.
subsystems.operation: Deploy and latch, then transfer between bars as robot attitude and support change.
subsystems.team_rationale: The flap helped avoid motor contact with the hangar wall when sharing with 254.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Shared hangar feasibility is a clearance problem across a swept volume. Static hook spacing cannot show the motor’s minimum wall clearance.
subsystems.interfaces: Partner location, motor protrusion and body swing interact during transfer.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Fixture-test failed latch engagement and representative partner clearances.
subsystems.unknowns: No rated loads, clearances or event success distribution.

revisions: Added back rollers and a ball blocker. The team placed the blocker between regional events with some uncertainty.
transferable_principles: Choose which mechanism owns the center before routing the rest of the robot.
Treat holding and release as separate modes and confirm that the handoff is safe after interruption.
disconfirming_conditions: Central climb loses its packaging advantage if other field constraints prevent side-by-side hanging.
Remote transmission is costly if the frame cannot preserve alignment or if shorter service intervals dominate.
remaining_gaps: As-built dimensions, original and revised release timing, and controlled shared-climb clearance.
recommended_images: Request a labeled top view of the cross-shaft and offset feed, plus side views of deployment and wall clearance.
